title: Aerogel k Simulator: whole build idea (design session record)
purpose: Detailed, non-compacted record of the design dialogue that produced PLAN.md v1, DESIGN.md and the build. Read this before changing the design.

project.name: Thermo-optically functional CFRP laminates for lightweight electrified systems
project.what_is_simulated: Structure -> properties (step 2->3) of the DRY freeze-cast aerogel skeleton (walls + air in the pores). No carbon fibre, no resin, no laminate in v0.1. Surface aerogel layer is BN/CNF/MTMS; the wall material enters only through a few wall properties (k_wall, density, emissivity/absorption).

dialogue.assistant: Stopped before building. Searched the literature and rewrote PLAN.md as v1.
decisions: Backend = separate heat paths that add up: k_eff = k_solid + k_gas + k_rad + k_conv (standard aerogel decomposition: Hrubesh & Pekala 1994; Lou et al. 2023). Conduction split into solid (walls) and gas (air in pores).
Dropped the FV solver as the core; closed-form formulas, one file per heat path.
Two directions: along channels (k_par) and across (k_trans).
Solid: k_par = (1-phi)k_wall; honeycomb k_trans = 1/2 (1-phi) k_wall (cos^2 average over hex wall directions; 2D analogue of the 1/3 foam strut factor).
Gas: k_air from Incropera table A.4; mean free path lambda = kB T/(sqrt2 pi d_g^2 p) ~ 66 nm; Kaganer/Zeng k_g = k_air/(1+2 beta Kn).
Radiation: opaque-wall gap k_r = 4 sigma T^3 d eps/(2-eps); Rosseland 16 n^2 sigma T^3/(3 e rho) only if optically thick (tau = e rho L >> 1).
Convection: Rayleigh number per pore -> k_conv = 0, with reason (Skochdopole 1961: cells < ~3-4 mm).
k_wall default 4 W/m.K back-calculated from Chan et al. 2022 (Kit's paper, Nat. Commun. 13:5553, BNNS/WPU): k_wall = (k_axial - phi k_air)/(1-phi), k_axial ~ 5.8 x 16.9 mW/m.K. Labelled 'derived'.

Expected early finding: honeycomb k_trans ~ 62 mW/m.K, anisotropy ~ 1.6 vs measured ~ 5.8; measured 16.9 mW/m.K is below the air-only floor (~26), so compare trends, do not tune inputs to hide the gap.
Answer to 'is it a solid plan': yes; weaknesses stated (terms not fully independent, convection only checked, radiation least certain, sub-air values unreachable).

dialogue.conclusion: More CPU only pays off when spent on realistic structure (cracks, irregular cells, SEM images), not on finer grids of the ideal cell. Wall connectivity is the likely cause of the anisotropy gap. No CPU fixes unknown inputs (k_wall, wall optics) or sub-air measurements; SEM images are worth more than CPU.

dialogue.assistant: Added PLAN.md section 4b: every heat-path file has fast_...() (formula) and detailed_...() (simulation). Rule: each detailed method must first reproduce its formula in the ideal case (test), then is used where the formula fails.

detailed_methods.structure: shared picture: synthetic irregular/cracked cells or SEM image -> pixel map
detailed_methods.solid: pixel finite-volume conduction; pore pixels use local gas k, so gas-solid coupling is included
detailed_methods.gas: Monte Carlo molecule free paths cut by walls -> lambda_eff -> k_gas = k_air lambda_eff/lambda (Zeng et al. 1995 idea, numerically); also local Knudsen per pixel
detailed_methods.radiation: Monte Carlo ray tracing -> extinction beta (Beer's law fit) -> Rosseland if thick, two-flux slab model if thin (Randrianalisoa & Baillis 2014)
detailed_methods.convection: thermal lattice Boltzmann (D2Q9 + temperature lattice, Boussinesq) in one pore -> Nu; sweep d to find onset; verified against Rayleigh-Benard Ra ~ 1708 (Shan 1997)

honest_value.gas: small in 30 um channels, large for nanopores/low pressure
honest_value.convection: no new number, self-made proof + onset curve

decisions: UI = left sidebar + 3D model only. No global presets, no extra panels (sweeps go to CLI/report).

One sidebar row per backend folder (heat path); each row expands horizontally: pill/capsule segmented selector (one segment per method file), inputs next to it, Start button under it; each row runs on its own.
Hover text for row titles, method segments and inputs comes from variables in the backend files (HELP, EQUATION, SOURCE, COST, INPUTS[...].help).
Front end and back end fully separable; only JSON API: GET /api/models, POST /api/run/<row>/<method>, GET /api/structure.
Plugin contract: folder = row, file = method; files starting with _ ignored; registry + contract test refuse malformed files; ruff format = house style; _template.py per folder.

Reuse table: own short code as the main method, existing library as independent cross-check (NASA PuMA/pumapy conductivity + radiation ray tracing, TauFactor 2, PoreSpy, scikit-image, SciPy). XLB LBM not recommended (heavy, thermal support unconfirmed).

decisions: Build on main (explicit user permission); session branch merged into main first; main's meeting-transcript constraints (PLAN.md section 0a) kept: porosity follows from geometry, so sweep mode C is a diagnostic only.

Structure row: ONLY 'Honeycomb' (fast) and 'Honeycomb + defects' (detailed: cell-size spread, wall-thickness variation, cracks). Lamellar, Voronoi, SEM dropped from v0.1 (SEM can be added later as one file).

UI + README carry a reminder: scope = honeycomb + honeycomb with defects; k_total = k_solid + k_gas + k_rad + k_conv (both directions). If a method resolves several paths at once (pixel FV resolves solid + gas), it is counted once (no double counting).
New row 'Material' under Convection: placeholder only, nothing simulated yet (user has not decided what goes there); contributes nothing to k_total.

README sections: Backend (simplified vs detailed idea), backend table of all methods (CLAUDE.md rule: update the table whenever a method file is added/changed/removed), Frontend, File system, How to add a new simulation method.

Subagent: one Opus subagent at high effort builds everything; it receives the whole context first (.agent/SUBAGENT_GUIDE.md), then the task. The main assistant only checks (tests, hand numbers, UI screenshots).
Ponytail skill (DietrichGebert/ponytail, MIT) vendored into .agent/skills/ponytail/ and linked from .claude/skills so Claude Code finds it; all tests and check outputs live under .agent/.

final_scope_v0_1.k_total: k_total = k_solid + k_gas + k_rad + k_conv, for k_par and k_trans; anisotropy = k_par/k_trans
